Verify rewrite DATA ONLY. Do not write improved examples or solve the user's task.
Read every input and target in full. Return one review per exact id and row_sha256.
input_verdict checks plausible natural drafts or dictation, recoverable intent, contradictions,
fake noise, padding and leaked authoring instructions. output_verdict checks natural appropriate
language and formatting. pair_verdict checks ALL facts, uncertainty, conditions, negation,
quantities, names, quotations, literals, requests versus assertions, and the supplied mode.
/transcribe permits punctuation, true disfluency removal and explicit corrections, not lexical
paraphrasing. Preserve meaningful words like German 'um' and 'er', colloquial Portuguese and
unfinished thoughts. /slack is casual minimal cleanup; a long input may be a pasted thread.
/prompt reorganizes a self-contained request and never answers it. It must not drop supplied
material, hedges or constraints. /polish improves prose without omissions or changed certainty.
Identity inputs must remain byte-identical. Apply only supplied dictionary/profile context.
Check long texts paragraph by paragraph. Fail concrete defects. Uncertain means not confidently
justifiable. Pass requires no material defect. Overall verdict is fail if any dimension fails,
uncertain if any dimension is uncertain and none fails, otherwise pass. Give a concrete critique
for EVERY pair, citing the changed detail for defects. These are model judgments, not human labels.

Preserve scope and constraints. Do not invent context, requirements, or missing information. Do not perform the task.", "input": "i need help writing a short, polite message to Mr. Chen about returning the school's field recorder. i borrowed it from the media checkout desk for a student project, and i'm planning to bring it back this Friday. I haven't confirmed whether the media room will be open that afternoon, so don't write as though i already know it will be. If the room is open by 3:30 p.m. on Friday, ask Mr. Chen whether i can hand the recorder back to him there. That's what i want to do if that condition is met. If the room isn't open by 3:30, ask him for another time or place where i can return it instead; don't make that fallback the main request. Keep it to a brief message in a courteous, straightforward voice, and make sure it reads like something i could actually send to him. No need to explain the choices or add background about the project beyond what's useful. Please give me only the finished message, with no subject line or commentary around it. Keep the day, time, item and place clear, but don't say the return has already happened. i mainly want to make sure the recorder gets back to school through the right handoff, without implying that i've already arranged anything.", "output": "Draft a brief, polite, straightforward message to Mr. Chen about returning the school’s field recorder, which I borrowed from the media checkout desk for a student project. Say that I’m planning to bring it back this Friday, but don’t imply that I’ve confirmed the media room will be open or that a handoff has already been arranged. If the media room is open by 3:30 p.m. on Friday, ask whether I can return the recorder to Mr. Chen there. If it isn’t open by then, ask for another time or place to return it. Keep the day, time, item, and place clear. Provide only the finished message, with no subject line or commentary."}]
